title: The Fall of Constantinople
description: April-May 1453. The player commands the last defenders of Byzantium under Constantine XI. Hold the Theodosian Walls against Mehmed II's siege: repair breaches from bombard fire, guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn, and survive repeated assaults. Defeat comes if the Hagia Sophia district falls; victory means holding until the final assault is broken.

issues_found: Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so neither the Byzantine defenders nor the Ottoman besiegers get their correct bonuses, unique units, or architecture set — an avoidable error since the engine ships both Byzantines and Turks.

The final-assault narration promises 'Janissaries, Sipahi cavalry and the whole Ottoman host', but the Ottoman roster contains only MAN_AT_ARMS x10 as infantry; the editor offers the Janissary (and Hand Cannoneer), so the Sultan's elite corps is represented by a Feudal-age generic swordsman.

The Golden Horn episode has no naval component whatsoever: no docks, no galleys, no transports, no fire ships for either side, despite the text describing ships dragged overland and 'Ottoman marines' probing the sea walls.
TREE_PALM_FOREST x6 is vegetation wrong for Thrace/the Bosphorus; a Mediterranean or oak/pine set would be plausible.

Defender force composition is too symmetrical: ~30 Byzantine units against ~32 Ottoman units, whereas the sources describe roughly 7,000 defenders against 60,000-80,000 besiegers; the disparity that defined the siege is absent.
Byzantine roster includes KNIGHT x4 and CHAMPION x1 but no gunpowder or Byzantine-flavoured troops; the Genoese contingent under Giustiniani is only implied by a renamed unit and a trigger.

Hagia Sophia is represented by a MONASTERY (two are placed), and the defeat trigger fires on a monastery generically — the engine offers the Wonder/temple objects that would read more clearly as the great church.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the Ottoman besiegers may appear as any culture and the Byzantine defenders lose their civ-specific walls/architecture — avoidable, since the engine ships both Byzantines and Turks

The narration promises 'Janissaries' in the final assault, but the Ottoman infantry placed are MAN_AT_ARMS x10 — the engine's Hand Cannoneer (or at minimum Two-Handed Swordsman/Champion) was available and is the standard stand-in for Janissaries

No ships, docks, or water-based force anywhere despite the Golden Horn sea-wall phase and the explicit reference to hauling the fleet overland; the 'Ottoman marines' arrive as land units created by trigger
TREE_PALM_FOREST and desert-style tents/pavilions give the map a Near-Eastern desert flavour rather than the Thracian/Marmara landscape of Constantinople
Ottoman host of roughly 27 units against a garrison of 30 badly misrepresents the historical disparity (~80,000 besiegers vs ~7,000 defenders); the besieger is not even numerically superior
Hagia Sophia is a MONASTERY (one of two identical ones), a weak signature for the city's cathedral when a Wonder or Cathedral-scale building was available
Only one gate pair and 49 wall segments stand in for the triple Theodosian line — no moat, no outer wall, no distinction between land and sea walls
Victory text asserts the city 'holds against the Sultan's host', a counterfactual outcome only lightly hedged by 'for another day'
